elaine: quick regional probe results for reranker+embed (384d). compared cpu vs gpu across us-east1 / us-west2 / eu-west1. short summary: gpu wins for low-latency single-request workloads; cpu can handle high-throughput batched offline workloads cheaper. sharing raw numbers and notes below.

kyle: can you paste the raw numbers and the exact bench command?

elaine: sure — command used:```
./run_bench --model rerank-384 --stage embed+rerank --dims 384 --batch 16 --concurrency 8 --device {cpu|gpu} --region {us-east1,us-west2,eu-west1} --kernel flash-attn-v2 --quant none
```

elaine: results (median throughput req/s, p95 latency ms):
```
US-EAST1  | GPU:  1120 rps  p95 62ms   | CPU: 420 rps  p95 140ms
US-WEST2  | GPU:  980 rps   p95 70ms   | CPU: 460 rps  p95 150ms
EU-WEST1  | GPU:  860 rps   p95 78ms   | CPU: 390 rps  p95 165ms
```

elaine: note these are embed+rerank end-to-end (embed dim 384, reranker on top). embed-only on GPU ~2400 rps at batch 32, cpu embed-only ~1200 rps at batch 64.

anil: what kernel/quant settings? any int8 runs? also curious about KV cache behavior for rerank.

elaine: kernel = flash-attn-v2 for GPU. fp16 on GPU. we did a small int8 quant run (post-training static int8) on eu-west1 GPU: throughput up ~12% but p95 tail +20ms in some cases — quality spot-checked looked OK but need a formal eval. KV cache: reranker uses short context, so KV not a major factor here.

maria: for capacity planning: baseline numbers per device (approx):
- p4d-ish GPU: 1k end-to-end rps (batch16), 2.4k embed-only rps (batch32)
- a10g/nvidia midsize: ~650 rps e2e
- 48-core cpu node: ~400 rps e2e at batch64 for embed-heavy flows
These assume steady-state warm workers and cold-starts avoided.

sam: how bad is the cold-start / p95 tail in apac? we saw PCIe tail and NUMA issues before.

elaine: apac (we tested ap-south1) had sporadic p95 spikes to 250ms for GPU e2e when first requests hit a node after scale-up — looks like PCIe init + kernel jit + small nvlink scheduling. warm steady-state p95 aligns with other regions. suggested mitigation: keep warm pool, quick fallback to smaller model, and async pre-warm for anticipated bursts.

kyle: for autoscaling rules, we should set expected per-GPU capacity to 900 rps (safe), use target_util 0.7, and burst_policy to allow extra nodes for 60s. thoughts?

maria: +1. also add a model-variant fallback (fp16 smaller reranker) for <200ms budget. use prefix caching for repeated queries to push effective throughput.

anil: plan for a follow-up: run int8 + kernel sweep (flash-attn-v2 vs fused-attn-v1) across regions, measure quality drift on our eval set, and capture per-token time breakdown (attention, softmax, matmul). I'll schedule a run.

ci-bot: bench-run-312 finished: https://ci.internal/bench-run-312 — artifacts uploaded (logs + raw CSV).

elaine: uploaded summary + csv to the eng-ml bench board. will kick off an int8 vs fp16 sweep tomorrow morning with the fused-attn comparison per anil. tagging @anil @maria. :rocket:

sam: awesome — can you also log the kernel env flags you used? we need to reproduce the p95 tail locally.

elaine: kernel flags in the artifact. quick paste:```
TF_KERNEL=flash-attn-v2
KERNEL_FLAGS=\"--use-fused-gemm --cuda-streams=2 --kv-cache=true\"
QUANT_MODE=none
```

kyle: thanks — will use the safe autoscale numbers for the capacity deck. closing loop after int8 sweep. :thumbsup:
